CHAPTER ONE Keep  T heir Heads Ringing Captain Blake Campbell leaned his chair back as he sipped appreciatively at the semi-clear liquid, wincing as it burned a trail of fire down his throat.  The face he made would be recognizable to anyone who had ever suffered the taste of cheap alcohol. Surveying the small crowd of heavily armed creatures, the yellow-blue hue of the planets sun played across the large blunt faces of the creatures now before him. Not for the first time that day ,  he marveled at how the hell he had gotten himself into this situation yet again. The  c aptain of the Revenant and her crew had been Rangers for just over a year. In that year ,  they had made friends and enemies alike,  a nd not all of them outside of the  r anks of their own organization.  A year ago, Blake and two other humans had been abducted from  Earth  by a desperate advanced  a rtificial  i ntelligence that Blake now shared his body and mind with. He and his fellow human crewmates , as well as a menagerie of aliens,  had come together, racing to stop the  Empire  from learning the location of Earth. They had failed. P erhaps  the Empire had not  yet  been to Earth or even knew the exact location of the planet, but  an infiltrator had removed the information  during the battle .  It was probable  they had the information, just that it was buried within a myriad of other data waiting to be discovered.  Ultimately, there was no way o f  knowing what the Empire knew.   Over the past year, he and his tight-knit warriors had developed a reputation for getting the job done in their unconventional way. So, when things got tough,  they  were sent in to salvage the situation.  This was  how he found himself here  o n this hot, humid world ,  babysitting the largest and ugliest things he had ever laid eyes on to date. Blake shook himself out of his reminisc ence  and focused on the deadly problem he now found himself in. His unnaturally silver eyes seemed to swirl with specs of black and grey as he regarded the creatures across the table  w hich, to his advantage ,  were unsettled by  the  ghostly effect. All the better to distract them from noticing the nervous glances he kept shooting their way.  They called themselves the Galuan. A predatory race who had the nasty habit of descending on unwary species in overwhelming numbers, taking over their planet, depleting it of resources while hunting down and killing the native population for sport and sustenance.  The creatures  could only be described as an unholy cross between a bat and an NFL linebacker , and they now  sat entirely too close for comfort . Blake tried to look relaxed despite the proximity of the creatures that loomed across from him at the small square table.  Apparently, they never learned the term 'personal space,'  he  thought ,  eyeing the closest of them.  He and his team had been sent to act as security for the planet’s ambassador. So now he sat, cooling his heels as said ambassador negotiated peace between themselves and the Galuans. The massive  b easts were well - armed and relaxed, secure in the fact that they had numbers and firepower on their side. The ir  circular blood - red eyes watched him intently as he regarded his glass. They never blinked or even appeared to breathe,  and  the effect  was  a little more than unsettling. “This is not bad, " Blake said casually as he took a hard swallow,   " but really ,  you guys need to learn how to age your liquor . ”  The Galuans considered any augmentations a weakness, so unlike the rest of the galaxy ,  they didn’t have translation nanites in their system. They just continued to stare at him with those beady red eyes, now beyond freaking him out and starting to disturb his calm.  Before Blake could think any more on those eyes, the communicator in his ear came to life ,  notifying him of an incoming message. He brushed the hair along the side of his head, subtly activating the device and spoke quietly.  “I am busy being sociable to the fucking gargoyle clan, so this had better be good , ”  h e whispered.  “Hey ,  Cap . S hit is about to get real down there. I just caught a direct burst transmission from the Galuan’s mothership hovering in orbit. Their orders are to terminate everyone , ” Kree, his team’s computer expert, said from his station aboard the  Revenant.  T he little furry being   sounded like  he might be in  a full- on conniption fit . The captain shook his head .   W hy is it every time we get called on a mission, things seemed to go to shi t?  h e thought ,  cursing under his breath. He quickly ran through the options in his head, settling on his last remaining ace in the hole. Blake quickly plucked a small black box with a single red button from his jacket pocket, causing some of the Galuans to twitch a little as his hand seemed to move faster than they could follow it , t hanks to his advanced nano treatments given to him by the  a rtificial  i ntelligence that resided within him .  Blake unceremoniously plopped the box on the table between himself and the creatures. “You know … I have this crazy - ass Russian on my ship. I mean he is really annoying sometimes, but I have to tell you, he makes some cool toys. Take this, for instanc e. L ooks pretty lame ,  right?”  h e asked . The  Galuans just cocked their heads, not unlike dogs hearing a high-pitched whistle . Man, these things creep me out ,  he thought with a slight shudder, doing his best not to show fear.  “But man, when I hit this button, this box is supposed to do something cool. You guys want to see?” Blake asked excitedly, fingering the little red button.  This instantly caught the attention of the group as their eyes studied the box intently. More curious than threatened by the little device.  “Do we know which one the leader is yet ? ” Blake whispered into the  comm. Rom's much deeper baritone answered  this time.   “Captain, I am at the southeast edge of the compound.   I have been studying the groups so far and have found no sign the leader is present.“ Blake cursed inwardly. That would have made this easier. The Galuans were a herd and tended to follow one leader. Remove that leader, and they froze up ,  not knowing what to do. However, understanding this weakness, they hid their leader well. “Rom ,  get ready to come in blazing . W e need to get the ambassador out of here in one piece. I will cause the distraction, and you go for the main building .   A ccording to my sensors ,   that's where  he is currently negotiating , ” Blake whispered ,  adding a bit too much sarcasm to that last word. Rom grunted in acknowledgment. Blake eyed the group of Galuans and started mentally picking his targets. As he did so ,  lines and probability statistics on his chances of killing  those  targets floated over the space between him and his guests, thanks to the optical nanites swimming in his cornea.  “Blake, these creatures’ anatomy is vastly different then you are used to, so the expected heart and headshots won’t kill them , ”  said  the soft female voice of Morgan, speaking within his own head. The  a rtificial  i ntelligence had made a bargain for pairing with the  c aptain , and h e now had access to her centuries of information and experience.  As he watched ,  areas of the Galuans began to highlight with yellow and red zones giving him target areas that ,  according to Morgan’s data ,  would do the most damage to the aliens.  “So, why is it a headshot or heart shot won’t kill them? I mean ,  they are bipedal creatures.” He mentally shot the question to her. “Because of their dense bone structure over sensitive areas ,  it 's  hard for kinetic or energy weapons to penetrate , ” her voice spoke in his head.  Blake nodded, accepting the answer and appreciating the visual targeting data she now fed to him. “Shira, you on the line?”  h e asked. “Right here ,  Cap , ”  s he said with the hum of engines in the background. “I am above you to the left.”  Blake’s eyes shift ed instinctively,   and he  cursed himself .   He knew   she was  cloaked , and  h e wouldn’t be able to see her anyway .   Hopefully he hadn't just  given the Galuans a clue as to what he was about to do. They might look stupid and brutish, but in packs, they were lethal warriors with amazing cunning.   This was supposed to be a simple negotiation. The Galuans had come to Previx and set up shop as they usually did,  but  the natives did not take kindly to this. And before the brutes could wipe out the planet’s population, their leadership had called in the Rangers to intervene. The egotistical ambassador had informed the team  that  they would wait outside with the rest of the help while he saved his people from certain doom, as he put it.  Now  we're  going to have to go in and save the little bastard ,  Blake thought ,  anger and irritation coming to an emotional crescendo. The indigenous population of Previx was  a bird-like species that reminded Blake of  o striches except with  four  legs and  six  arms .   T hey  even  reacted the same when threatened :   s tuck their head s  in the sand and waited for the danger to pass.  This made Blake smile as he thought about the smug ambassador sticking his head in the dirt. He sighed loudly.  So much for an easy day drinking with the boys,  he thought. “Shira , ” he said ,  now loud enough for the Galuans to hear as their own communicators squawked ,  and guns began to raise bearing down on Blake.  “Keep their heads ringing,”  h e said as he hit the button on the box that Davi had given him, and nothing happened. The  e ars on the nearest of the Galuan’s perked up, almost looking like a curious  p it  b ull as Blake cursed and hit the button again. The  c reatures, now sensing something was amiss ,  leveled their guns at Blake ,  who held up a hand in a stop gesture towards the largest of the creatures.  “Hold the fuck on ,  Brutus!”  h e laughed ,  “You ever just have one of those days, where no matter what you do ,  everything goes tits up?” Brutus’ face hardened with homicidal resolve  a s  his finger snugged  the trigger on his weapon. Blake’s world came alive as the nanites in his mind began to process  at lightning speed  everything his senses were receiving .  He could make out the individual muscles along Brutus’ finger as it tensed against the trigger ,  slowly moving to activate the weapon and end his life in a hail of crimson plasma fire. He had time to reflect on just what a crappy day it was and how he was going to shove that little box  up Davi’s ass when he got back on board the ship. With supernaturally fast reflexes, another of the gifts he had received when pairing with Morgan, he kicked the table up ,  causing the black box to fly  into the air.  Some of  the Galuans   t ook  their attention off the human for a moment as their eyes followed the arcing box.  That was all he needed . W ith nanite-infused superhuman speed ,  Blake pulled the two large revolver - like plasma hand cannons from his gun belt ,  and before the creatures could get off a shot ,  Blake pushed himself backward ,  riding the rickety chair towards the ground and firing into the eager killers. As soon as he felt the back of the chair hit the stone, he kicked the edge of the table hard,   sending it flying into the murderous group , d istracting them as they tried to dodge the fast - flying furniture. At the same moment ,  Rom exploded from the tree line, helmet up and roaring like a T-Rex. He was an imposing figure at over seven feet tall and as wide as a bus ,   with  blood - red skin  and l arge black horns .   They  curl ed  around the edges of his head ,  coming to two points on either side of his large fanged mouth ,   and his sharp elongated talons tightly gripped  his over-sized automatic plasma shotgun . Some of the Galuans turned their guns towards Rom as he bounded at the main building . A  hail of red plasma rounds exploded from  his  shotgun’s barrel at twenty shots a second ,  mowing down anything unfortunate enough to be in his path. Blake had been hesitant to have Rom use  the shotgun for fear it had a limited range, but seeing it spewing death to enemies forty feet away ,  he gladly stood corrected. As Galuans turned to fire, Blake’s two massive hand cannons sounded off,  cutting  down half of the enemy guard contingent before they had even turned back to face him. He pushed on the discarded table that had dropped between them, breaking their sightline. Those still standing began shredding the table with plasma fire trying to kill the lone human. They were so focused on him ,  none of them noticed the air shimmer behind them as a ship appeared where a second ago there had been nothing. The Spector gunship’s chameleon hull plating  dis solved to black ,  now displaying the lethal vessel with its two large front cannons ,  belching crimson plasma. He watched in a mix of awe and disgust as the creatures were blown apart by the computer targeted surgical blasts. From the ship’s booming speaker, a man's deep voice bellowed .  “Thank God it’s Friday.”  A nd the beat of Dr. Dre’s  " Keep  T heir Heads Ringing "  resounded over the field like a war cry. Blake’s hand cannons  sang  along to the beat, as the remaining guards emerged from the shacks and wood-line, the combined firepower of the three Rangers silencing them before weapons could even be drawn. Blake tapped his com m .   “Shira, watch the perimeter .  I don’t want any of these fuckers getting away, or we will be back here in a month. They breed like damn rabbits. Oh,  and if someone could find me the leader! " Blake barked sarcastically.   " Yeah, that would be awesome.”  Sending a thought to his boots, he activated the gravity repulsors ,  instantly decreasing his weight by half. Blake easily launched his much lighter self over the edge of the building the enemy had used as a guard post.   He  landed deftly on the ground next to a very surprised Galuan guard. “ S ' up , ” he greeted,  n odding at him casually ,   then p unching  his fist through the surprised creature’s chest before it had the chance to react. The guard slid off Blake’s metal arm with a wet sound.  He quickly reset his weight, shaking the disgusting mess off his arm,  and  ran to catch up with Rom, who was just about to the entrance of the building that housed the negotiations. The single-story squat structure had at one time been a bomb shelter until the Galuans had landed and declared the duracrete fortress their base. Looking at the building with the help of Morgan’s access to his optical nanite sensors and her centuries of tactical knowledge, the frame around the  sizeabl e wood - like door highlighted for him.  “Blake, looking at the microfractures around the frame and the age of the door itself, it looks as if someone has tried in the recent past to batter it down, there is an eighty-three percent chan c e that you and Romulax, with enough force ,  will be able to shatter the organic material that it’s made out of , ”  Morgan said  to Blake mentally.  He sent her a nod back to acknowledge  her advice . I t sounded good to him.   He really didn’t have any other plan to get in there except to have Shira blast the crap out of the structure until it collapsed.  Blake came up alongside his friend and crewmate  and slapped  him on the bac k, b oth to say hi and let the big man know he was there.   “Ready to be a battering ram , ” he asked his friend as he pointed at the door. Rom looked at him ,  confused for a moment, but Blake could see the moment when he comprehended what he wanted to do his face broke into a mildly concerned look. “Don’t worry, it was recommended , ”  h e told him, his way of letting him know it was a Morgan - idea and not his. For some reason ,  that made all the difference because it instantly put the big creature at ease.  My plans aren’t that bad ,  he thought irritably but caught the tail end of Morgan’s mental chuckle at the thought. He shook his head .  S he 's  probably right ,  he thought and let it go. “See, I like it when we are subtle and shit , ” Blake said ,  smiling at Rom. With a thought ,  his helmet segments flow ed  from the armor’s collar ,  moved up over the previous one ,  and locked into place ,  covering his entire head . I n seconds ,  the eye sockets  began   to glow red as the heads-up display came online. “Cap, from the sensors ,  it looks like the Ambassador is still alive and in the room on the east side of the building. Be aware there are lots of those bastards between you and him , ” Kree announced in his ear. “Dude, can you do anything about giving us a little edge in that building , ” Blake inquired as he and Rom sped up and hit the  large door ,  full force.  Their armor took the brunt of the impact , sending the door exploding inward. Wood-like shards turned to small deadly projectiles that embedded themselves into the Galuans waiting within. Kree sat at his console on the Revenant, a set of silver nanite tendrils leading from the terminal to his cranium ,  tapping directly into the quantum supercomputer he had installed into a part of his brain. His eyes went distant and seemed to fog over as code and information began to scroll in the air in front of him ,  put there by the optical nanites at the speed of thought. Within nanoseconds, he found the piece of code he  was  searching for , m ade a quick edit by merely thinking it ,  and tapped his communicator. “Cap, the lights will go out in five seconds, the n the  fire suppression system will trigger within two second s . A fter that ,  every door will unlock, and all alarms will start sounding at once . ” Blake smiled.  Damn that little furry bastard is handy as hell ,  h e thought as he leveled the pistols and fired into the emerging guards as they came to investigate the ruckus. He could see the red blasts of Rom’s shotgun as he began the slaughter. Death came quickly to every Galuan who emerged into the large antechamber.  The pair of executioners were bathed in the hue of crimson plasmablasts as the lights went out ,  right on time.  C hemicals began pouring from the ceiling like a thick blue fog   layering the floor ,  giving the room an eerie cemetery - like feel as the pair continued to deal  death . Suddenly ,  as promised, every alarm in the place began to sound ,  causing the Galuans to drop their weapons and grab their heads ,   pained by the noise as if they were  the bats they resembled . T hey had incredibly sensitive hearing ,  and the sounds coming out of the terminals acted like daggers embedding into their heads. The two armored Rangers made their way through the building until they came to the room that held the ambassador. Entering, they came upon a much larger Galuan ,  standing behind the shaking ostrich-like creature ,  a pistol held to the side of the ambassador’s head and ,  not considering the significant size discrepancy between the two of them, tried to use the much smaller creature as a shield. Rom paused and turned to Blake.   “Hey, I think we found the leader , ”  h e said excitedly. Blake shook his head . S ometimes he forgot this great scary being could act so childlike. “No shi t. Y ou think ? ” Blake retorted.  The large Galuan pushed  its   black pistol against the side of the  a mbassador’s head. Fear was radiating off the lanky feathered creature in waves. A deep rumbling voice erupted from his more massive captor .  “I get to walk out, or you will be picking up his brai-” Blake wheeled on him.   “Hey ,  Dracula, shut the fuck up . C an’t you see the adults are talking ? ” The  c reature looked puzzled as the  ambassador's  mobile translator reiterated his message in the Galuan’s native language.   Blake turned back to Rom. “Anyway, when I ask if you have seen the leader ,  you really don’t have to tell me when I am standing right here. That will get you the title  ' Captain Obvious, '  and you really don’t want that ,  do you ? ” Blake chided . Rom return ed  a reproachful look to his captain.   “Most definitely not .   B esides ,  I thought that was Kree’s name.” Blake gave him a pitying loo k .   “Hey ,  if it fits… tha t’s all I am saying . A nd no one wants that ,  big guy.” Blake slapped him on the shoulder . The  Galuan squeeze d  his trigger,   having had enough of the two being s'  conversation. Blake, in one fluid motion ,  snapped his pistol up and  blew   a  massiv e hole in the Galuan leader. Everything above his eyes disintegrating into a fine green mist.  The pistol smoked,  now  overheated, out of power ,  and useless .  Morgan had instantly increased the output to compensate for the cranial bone armor of the Galuan , leaving it exhausted . A small snicker  from  Rom  drew Blake's attention to   a   puddle   of bright pink fluid at the  ambassador's  three-toed feet .   The bird's  eyes ,  as wide as dinner  plates ,   met  Blake 's  incredulous  stare.   He  shook his head as if not really believing what he was seeing.  “Did you really just wet yourself?”  Blake  asked the bird. The  a mbassador  scraped together  what little self-respect he had left ,  realizing the immediate danger was over ,  puffed out his bird chest ,  and walked confidently past the two gawking Rangers. “You will escort me out now, and no one  - I mean  no one -   will speak of this  ever! ”  He leveled his best I - am - a - mean - chicken look at Blake ,  who still held an amazed expression as the Ambassador strolled by  them . Blake turned to Rom ,  who returned the look with a shrug. “Beings deal with fear differently . M aybe that was his race’s defense mechanism.”  Blake ,  shaking his head, motioned for Rom to join him ,  and they both followed the  a mbassador out of the building doing their best to avoid the wet prints left by the ambassador and towards the waiting Specter.  Rom slapped Blake on the back.   “He really pissed himself , ” Rom said in awe, and they both cracked up like adolescent school kids.   CHAPTER TWO All the General’s Men The  g rand  c hancellor and  g eneral for the Rangers sat alone in his dimly lit office. A year ago, he had just been a simple temple monk, but because of circumstances beyond his control ,  he  had  paired with an ancient artificial intelligence. One that had spent centuries as a great general, now th e  simple monk and spiritual leader had found himself in control of the most advanced and effective fighting force in the galaxy. The Rangers had done well spreading their influence from system to system , p ushing back the Empire and saving planets and races from slavery … until now. Now he finally felt in over his head, as if the old argument of  his unworthiness  of the position was finally being realized. Spread across his desk were a series of reports that, for the last five hours, he had read and re-read, trying to divine something to explain what should have been impossible. Five Vega - class Ranger destroyers and their crews, gone. No communication and no trace of any of them. Pouring over even the mundane sections of the ship ' s communications logs ,  he could find nothing to explain it. Everything had been routine up until the moment when it hadn’t and then …n othing. This was not possible, no ship in known space could take a Vega - class destroyer much less take it so fast that not one of them had been able to launch a communication probe or get off a distress signal. He stared from one report to the other with a troubled look on his face as he carefully re-read each set of details again, something tickled his subconscious but refusing to reveal itself , i nstead lurking right out of reach of his conscious thoughts. He just couldn’t put his finger on it. “Look at the geographic locations, there is a pattern there , ”  s aid a whispered voice from within his head. Forsaken, the  a rtificial  i ntelligence who also inhabited the general’s body, mentally nudged him towards the holo-viewer. Forsaken was his conscience , t he voice  whispering  in his ear ,  guiding him when he needed it. This being one of those times ,  Seafu felt the white fur along his back and neck bristle and then settle again. Forsaken was ancient with an immeasurable amount of knowledge and experience ,  both at Seafu’s disposal . T he only cost was that he had to share his mind with the being. Sometimes that  was  sti ll  unsettling as the pairing gave both entities access to the vast neural pathways that held memories and experiences from Seafu’s life . B ut that path was a two-way street. Seafu had access to  all  Forsaken’s centuries of experience and memories as well ,  which included the experience and memories of all the beings that Forsaken had previously paired with. The AI acted as a curator and librarian.  Delivering needed knowledge and experience, thus sparing Seafu from the psychotic break that would occur should the information just be dumped into his mind. The ancient race that had created the boxes discovered early on that giving someone access to the personality, experience, and life of another would cause the mind to reject it and fracture. Thus, the  a rtificial  i ntelligence was the gateway to that knowledge. Seafu took another look at the locations of the incidents and then started to see a pattern. Pulling up a holographic map on his large grey stone desk ,  he tapped the locations which highlighted as his finger connected with each. “ C omputer ,  connect all locations , ”  h e said thoughtfully, and as he watched a line began to form between each of the ship ' s last known positions . A nd there it was . T he incidents formed a direct line. Seafu studied the galaxy map looking for where the next incident would happen.  Who could be doing this ,  and what  is  the ir  end game ?  he thought. “Croatoan , ”  F orsaken whispered into Seafu’s mind. He followed the line and  found the point , the planet that held the old archive for the temple as well as a current colony of displaced humans that had been removed from  E arth as slaves. Studying the highlighted route, he attempted to divine actions or motivation of this unknown threat.  “How did this planet factor in?"  h e  asked himself  aloud . Croatoan had been the site of a battle that, had it succeeded ,  would have given the Empire the location of  Earth . Blake Campbell and  his  crew had thwarted this attempt , s aving not only the location of his home planet but also the base  where  Seafu now resided. Seafu accessed his nanite communications implant and summoned his assistant ,  w hom ,  to his credit ,   entered  the office before Seafu had closed the connection. “Yes, sir ,  what may I do for you?”  a sked the young initiate ,  his yellow  eye- slits seeming to glow a light crimson as the subdued light in the room reflected off  his retinas . The  i nitiate ' s scaly blue skin seemed to accent this effect giving him a very lizard-like visage. Sirocco had been with Seafu since he had taken on the position  as l eader of the Rangers. He was incredibly efficient ,  and if Seafu was totally honest with himself ,  the only reason he hadn’t failed administratively. For a secret organization, it was amazing the amount of paperwork that they generated. “I need you to contact our  f orward operations base on Croatoan and see if there has been anything, and I mean  anything  out of the ordinary. I also need to speak with Colonel Heroshi as soon as  it  is convenient. We might have a credible threat against his sector , ” Seafu stated to the young initiate , w ho bowed slightly and left the room. Heroshi was the commanding officer at the forward post, and if anyone  kne w what was happening in that area, it would be him. Seafu sat back in his chair . T his was a threat they were unprepared for. Since the beginning  of the Rangers last year, not one ship they had stood against had even come close to defeating the advanced systems and  technologies  left to them by the ancients. If something was out there that could so easily best them, then they needed to know what it was. They were being hunted, and this unseen enemy was already winning. Seafu’s thoughts were interrupted by a communication ping. Captain Blake Campbell was calling in. Seafu had been waiting for this call for the last two days. Blake and his crew might have been unorthodox, paranoid ,  and an all-around pain in his ass, but they were effective and excelled at handling the next to impossible tasks that sometimes the Rangers were called upon to perform. Blake had very few friends on the council, but that can happen when you point loaded weapons at people who were unaccustomed to not getting their way. Had it not been for Seafu’s staunch support of the crew, it was very likely they would have been drummed out. Even with their success rate, some council members had very long memories when it came to holding a grudge. Seafu reached out with his mind using his nanites connected to the wireless communication node in his office, a trick Forsaken had taught him  and one  which came in quite handy. Closing his eyes, a scene materialized before him as if he was  there . He was standing in front of Blake in the captain’s stateroom onboard the Revenant. “Hello ,  Captain .  I trust you are calling with good news for me?” Seafu said ,  already having read the draft report that had come  through his office six hours ago.  Blake shifted uncomfortably.   “Well ,  boss ,  if you read the report  - w hich I am assuming you did   -   y ou know the ambassador is alive, and we managed to diffuse the situation on the planet. I have high confidence those damn pests will be leaving the planet now that their leader has been retired and most of their forces terminated . Still,  I am sure the ambassador himself might be lodging a formal complaint against the Rangers for what I think he said was ‘high - handed tactics.’ Unfortunately, it was hard to make out in between the whining and crying he was doing , ” Blake stated while purposely not looking at the hologram of his boss. Seafu smiled, having already received a call from the government of the ambassador ,  asking that Blake put in a formal apology for said tactics. To  that  complaint ,  Seafu not so gently reminded them that without those tactics ,  the ambassador would be dead, and the planet would have been doomed to remain in possession of the creatures that they so desperately wanted to be rid of. They acquiesced the ir  demand quickly when Seafu hinted that he would be happy to pull Ranger support for their area if they pushed the request. “Yes, Captain .  I have already spoken to the sitting government and smoothed it over. I would ask again that you show a little more diplomacy when dealing with leadership and public figures on a planet. This not being the first time a sitting government or public official felt you were…less than respectfu l, ” Seafu admonished his captain ,  though not  without a smile. An innocent look came over Blake's face.   “Hey, I am the poster child for  d iplomacy. I can’t help if most of the officials we deal with are complete cowards who seem to think that everything will be okay .  If everyone would just listen to them and stop thinking on their own , ” Blake responded ,  looking directly at the hologram. Seafu rolled his eyes.   “Please ,  Blake, just try to make my job a little less like presiding over a preschool class and more like the military outfit we claim to be.” He smiled.   “N ow   -   with that dressing down completed   -   h ow is my daughter doing?” They spent the next few minutes talking about Xera. Seafu  was  enraptured when listening to her adventures onboard the ship and asked follow - up questions when he had them. Once  t he y  had finished catching up  about  his adopted daughter , t he  general ’s whole demeanor changed .  “Blake, I might have a job for you. I need you to standby there for twelve hours until I can confirm a few things.
